exposure: diagnosis of cervical cancer during pregnancy
cohort: The study included 9,096,788 pregnant women with pregnancies at 24 weeks or above, who delivered a child or experienced maternal death between 2004-2014, including 222 diagnosed with cervical cancer prior to delivery.
finding: Cervical cancer during pregnancy is associated with significant maternal and delivery risks, including higher rates of preterm delivery, cesarean section, and severe complications, but neonatal outcomes were largely unaffected.
mod_finding: Women with cervical cancer during pregnancy had significantly higher rates of cesarean section compared to those without cervical cancer.
